thesis: An-Nahl converts the catalogue of visible mercies (varied colors, the sea's food/adornment/commerce, mountains, rivers, roads, landmarks, stars) into a tawhid argument that culminates in the question 'is the One who creates like one who does not create?' and closes on the uncountability of Allah's favor met by His forgiveness.
notes: Clean. The organizing claim is al-Tabari's own framing of 16:17 almost point for point: he addresses the passage to the idol-worshippers ('afaman yakhluqu hadhihi al-khala'iq al-'ajibah allati 'addadnaha 'alaykum ... kaman la yakhluqu shay'an'), i.e. the enumerated creations are marshalled as the premise of the tawhid question — which is exactly the file's 'courtroom of tawhid' hook. Theme 2 (incomplete gratitude met by forgiveness) is carried verbatim by all four: al-Tabari 'la tutiqu ada' shukriha ... lam kana minkum min taqsir fi shukr ... idha tubtum'; Ibn Kathir quotes Ibn Jarir to the same effect; al-Muyassar 'yatajawaz 'an taqsirikum fi ada' shukr al-ni'am'; al-Jalalayn 'fadlan an tutiqu shukraha'. Lexical glosses all check out: dhara'a = khalaqa (al-Tabari/al-Jalalayn), mukhtalifan alwanuhu = animals/trees/fruits/minerals (Qatadah, al-Muyassar), lahman tariyyan = fish, hilyah = pearl and coral (al-Tabari), mawakhir = cleaving the water ('Ikrimah 'tashuqquhu', Ibn Kathir 'plowing'). Notably the file makes NO countable/absolute claims at all (no 'only', 'never', 'N times', 'hapax') and NO named-source attributions, so checks 2 and 3 have no exposure. No ahkam content, no quoted tafsir, hence no truncation artifact. Only optional improvement for the human: al-Tabari records real ikhtilaf on mawakhir (mawaqir/laden vs. cleaving vs. sailing crosswise vs. running both directions on one wind) and the file presents 'cleaving' as if settled — harmless for a non-ahkam lexical point, but a one-clause hedge would make it airtight.

thesis: The passage moves Bani Israel from al-'adhab al-muhin (the punishment that makes low) to al-bala' al-mubin (the testing that makes clear) — one letter apart, both Form IV active participles — so that what rescue hands you is itself an examination, and the commentators refuse to narrow that examination to hardship.
notes: Strongest file in the group; every tafsir attribution is verbatim-accurate against the fetched text, including the Arabic it quotes. Spot-verified: al-Jalalayn 44:33 = 'ni'mah zahirah min falq al-bahr wa-l-mann wa-l-salwa wa-ghayriha' (file's 'a manifest favour ... the splitting of the sea, the manna, the quails, and the rest') EXACT; al-Tabari 'wa-khtalafa ahl al-ta'wil fi dhalika al-bala'' EXACT; Qatadah's list ('anjahum Allah min 'aduwwihim, thumma aqta'ahum al-bahr, wa-zallala 'alayhim al-ghamam, wa-anzala 'alayhim al-mann wa-l-salwa') EXACT; Ibn Zayd 'bal ibtalahum bi-l-rakha' wa-l-shiddah' plus his citation of 21:35 EXACT; al-Tabari's refusal 'lam yada' lana dalilan min khabar wa-la 'aql' EXACT; his gloss 'ma fihi ikhtibar yubayyinu li-man ta'ammalahu annahu ikhtibar' EXACT; al-Muyassar 'ibtila'uhum wa-khtibaruhum; rakha' wa-shiddah' EXACT; al-Jalalayn 'alimi zamanihim ay al-'uqala'' EXACT; al-Jalalayn on 'ala 'ilm = 'minna bi-halihim' EXACT. Morphology verified against the corpus cache, not just the file's own tags: najjayna VF:2 (Form II), muhin ACT_PCPL VF:4 root هون, mubin ACT_PCPL VF:4 root بين — so 'both active participles built on the causative mould' is literally true; 'ali ACT_PCPL; ikhtarnahum VF:8 (Form VIII); 'ilm and 'alamin both ROOT:علم in 44:32; 'ala occurs exactly twice in 44:32; three divine verbs (najjayna / ikhtarnahum / ataynahum) confirmed. Uthmani text confirms the bookends: 44:30 terminates on المهين and 44:33 terminates on مبين. ADAB — this is a chosenness passage and the file handles it correctly: it carries the classical limiter ('above the worlds of THEIR OWN TIME') and is right that all four editions have it (al-Tabari 'alami ahl zamanihim yawma'idhin, al-Muyassar 'alami zamanihim, al-Jalalayn 'alimi zamanihim, Ibn Kathir via Mujahid/Qatadah), it preserves al-Tabari's refusal to narrow bala' instead of flattening it to hardship, and it frames the calf as 'the shadow that must be acknowledged inside a longer story' rather than as supersessionist verdict. ONE PHRASING NIT, not a claim failure, for the human's copy pass: twice the file says the passage 'ends ... on the word bala'' ('And it ends — look at the last word — on the word **bala'**' and 'look at its last word before anything else'), but the terminal word of 44:33 is مبين — bala'un mubin is the closing PHRASE. The file's actual load-bearing claim (mubin as the terminal bookend answering muhin) is correct, so nothing substantive rests on the slip; 'ends on the phrase bala'un mubin' fixes it.

thesis: 41:53 announces an ongoing divine 'evidence program' — signs engineered in the cosmos and in the self, unfolding across centuries of human discovery until truth self-clarifies — after which Allah turns away from the doubter to tell the believer that His own witnessing was always sufficient.

flags.quote: **Stage 3 — The truth.** ٱلْحَقُّ — THE truth, with the definite article. Not a truth. Not your truth. THE truth. The signs have pointed from the edge of the universe through the self to arrive at this: a singular, definite, non-negotiable reality.
flags.issue: The referent of the pronoun in أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ is glossed by all four editions, unanimously and without ikhtilaf, as THE QUR'AN — not truth-in-general. al-Jalalayn: ﴿حتى يتبين لهم أنه﴾ أي القرآن ﴿الحق﴾ المنزل من الله. Ibn Kathir: 'until it becomes manifest to them that this (the Qur'an) is the truth.' al-Muyassar: أن القرآن الكريم هو الحق الموحى به من رب العالمين. al-Tabari: حتى يعلموا حقيقة ما أنزلنا إلى محمد. The file never once says the verse is about the Qur'an; it recasts the whole ayah as a generic proof-of-God program addressed to 'the modern skeptic.' This is the organizing frame of the file, so the miss propagates through every section.

flags.quote:
And then Allah turns away from the doubter.

He turns to His Prophet ﷺ — to the one who already believes — and asks a rhetorical question that reframes everything ... The doubter gets the evidence program. The believer gets the Witness.
flags.issue: This inverts the classical reading of أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ. al-Muyassar reads the sufficiency as directed AT the deniers and as proof of the Prophet's truthfulness: أولم يكفهم دليلًا على أن القرآن حق، ومَن جاء به صادق، شهادة الله تعالى؟ al-Jalalayn likewise: أو لم يكفهم في صدقك أن ربك لا يغيب عنه شيء ما. Ibn Kathir: Allah 'bears witness that Muhammad ﷺ is telling the truth in what he says' (citing 4:166). al-Tabari reads it as the Prophet being told that Allah witnesses all his creatures' deeds and will requite them. Not one of the four turns the question into consolation for a believer who no longer needs the evidence. The genitive كَ in بِرَبِّكَ does address the Prophet, but the sufficiency is offered as evidence FOR THEM, not as a private reassurance that replaces evidence. This is the file's named Theme 2 and its closing synthesis.

flags.quote: The entire history of human discovery — every telescope that revealed the vastness of the cosmos, every microscope that showed the impossible precision of a cell, every moment a human being sat in silence and felt the weight of their own consciousness — all of it is captured in the movement from سَنُرِيهِمْ to يَتَبَيَّنَ.
flags.issue: This is the soft i'jaz 'ilmi bridge the house style quarantines, and it is asserted as the ayah's meaning, not flagged as a contemporary extension — reinforced by 'ٱلْـَٔافَاقِ ... The edge of the observable universe' and 'Scientists feel it when they discover a pattern too elegant to be random.' Two problems. (1) No edition supports extending the promise across centuries of scientific discovery; al-Jalalayn (النيرات والنبات والأشجار / لطيف الصنعة وبديع الحكمة), al-Muyassar (أقطار السموات والأرض ... بديع آيات الله) and Ibn Kathir's secondary reading ('man and his physical composition ... the science of anatomy') warrant a cosmos-and-self reading, but as present observable signs, not a future research programme. (2) al-Tabari explicitly REJECTS the cosmic reading and gives his reason: he reports it from Ibn Zayd (آفاق السموات: نجومها وشمسها وقمرها), then rules وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الأول — because 'غير معقول أن يكون تهدّدهم بأن يريهم ما هم راءوه' (they already saw the stars, sun and moon constantly, so a promise to SHOW them cannot mean those). The file's future-unfolding-discovery frame is precisely the reading al-Tabari argues against, and the file mentions none of this. To PASS, the horizons-of-discovery material needs an explicit reflection flag AND the file must carry the majority reading it currently omits entirely: آفاق = the Prophet's victories in the regions around Makkah, أنفسهم = the conquest of Makkah (al-Tabari's choice, via al-Suddi and al-Minhal; Ibn Kathir's primary, via Mujahid, al-Hasan and al-Suddi: Badr and the conquest of Makkah).

flags.quote: They've put their fingers in their ears — literally described in this surah — and wrapped themselves in their garments to avoid hearing the message.
flags.issue: False as stated, verified mechanically against the Uthmani text (node_modules/quran-validator/data/quran-verses.json, normalized: harakat and waqf marks stripped, alif variants folded, whitespace collapsed). أَصَٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ occurs at 2:19 and 71:7 only; ٱسْتَغْشَوْا۟ ثِيَابَهُمْ occurs at 71:7 only. Neither phrase occurs anywhere in Surah Fussilat — a scan of all 54 ayahs returns only 41:44 (فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ), which is deafness, not fingers. What Fussilat actually reports is 41:5: قُلُوبُنَا فِىٓ أَكِنَّةٍ ... وَفِىٓ ءَاذَانِنَا وَقْرٌ وَمِنۢ بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ. The imagery has been imported from Nuh 71:7 and asserted as 'literally described in this surah.'

flags.quote: Something happens in the second half of this ayah that most people read right past. It's one of those shifts that is invisible in English but unmistakable in Arabic.
flags.issue: Two-part overstatement. (a) بِرَبِّكَ is rendered 'your Lord' in every standard English translation, so the shift is not invisible in English. (b) The second-person address to the Prophet is not introduced here: the immediately preceding ayah 41:52 opens with قُلْ (corpus: IMPV|VF:1|2MS), so the Prophet is already the addressee going into 41:53. Calling the person-change 'iltifat' is at best loose, since iltifat proper is a shift of reference to the SAME referent, whereas here the third-person deniers and the second-person Prophet are different referents. The observation that the ayah's two halves face different parties is fine; the framing around it is not.

notes: Answering the review question directly: YES, the file reads 41:53 as an unfolding prophecy of modern discovery (telescopes, microscopes, 'the edge of the observable universe', 'the entire history of human discovery', 'a promise that has not expired ... the program is still running'), and NO, it is nowhere flagged as an extension — it is asserted as the verse's meaning and hard-coded into the frontmatter theme ('The Two Theaters'). It stops short of full i'jaz 'ilmi (no specific scientific finding is claimed to be predicted, no 'science proves the Qur'an'), so this is the soft form — but unquarantined, and made worse by the fact that al-Tabari argues against exactly this reading. THE FIX, in order of priority: (1) restore the Qur'an as the referent of أنه الحق — the ayah is about the Qur'an's truth being vindicated, and the file currently never says so; (2) rewrite Part 1 §III and Theme 2 — أولم يكف is evidence offered TO the deniers of the Prophet's truthfulness (al-Muyassar, al-Jalalayn, Ibn Kathir), not a private sufficiency granted to the believer in place of evidence; (3) add the majority historical reading (conquests / fath Makkah) and al-Tabari's stated rejection of the cosmic reading, then re-flag the horizons-of-discovery material as contemplation rather than tafsir; (4) delete or relocate the 'fingers in their ears / wrapped in their garments' sentence (that is Nuh 71:7, not Fussilat; Fussilat's own line is 41:5); (5) soften the iltifat paragraph. WHAT VERIFIES CLEANLY, so the human does not re-do it: every morphological claim checks out against scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json — سَنُرِيهِمْ IMPF|VF:4 root رأي (Form IV causative, plus the future sin as a separate FUT prefix segment), يَتَبَيَّنَ IMPF|VF:5 root بين (Form V), شَهِيدٌ tagged ADJ fa'il root شهد (the file's step0 table and the corpus agree; only the inline morphology comment says pos=N), ٱلْـَٔافَاقِ root أفق, أَنفُسِهِمْ root نفس, يَكْفِ root كفي. Contextual claims verify too: 41:26 quoted accurately (لَا تَسْمَعُوا۟ لِهَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانِ وَٱلْغَوْا۟ فِيهِ), 'Ad and Thamud are in the surah (41:13-17), the skins testifying are in the surah (41:20-22), 90:4 kabad and 12:53 ammarah bi-l-su' are both accurate. One unverifiable absolute left standing, not counted as failed: 'it does something almost no ayah in the Quran does in exactly this way' — no mechanical test can settle it; recommend cutting it. All four tafsir editions fetched successfully for this ayah, so nothing here rests on a failed fetch, and no truncation artifacts were present (the file quotes no tafsir text at all — which is itself the root problem: none of the four editions is engaged anywhere in 3,870 words).
